## Overview

**In plain terms.** This is the mandatory response-link companion to `lrp-rli-itt-008`. It asks how much the estimated randomised-arm contrast in phoneme blending changes when the model respects the test's one-in-three guessing level. It is a robustness analysis, not a second independent experiment or a replacement outcome.

The analysis rows, treatment coding, own-baseline and age precision terms, priors, sampling configuration, diagnostics and available-case causal assumptions match the primary B model. Random assignment created exchangeability in the original cohort, but conditioning on archive inclusion and observed analytic variables can break it. Reading even the fitted-sample contrast causally therefore assumes that selection did not depend jointly on assigned arm and potential outcomes; extending it to all 57 randomised children requires further missing-data assumptions and sensitivity.

## Model

The linear predictor is identical to the primary model:

$$
\eta_i = \alpha + \tau\, G_i
       + \gamma_{\text{own}}\, \operatorname{logit}_*(B_{\text{pre},i}, N)
       + \gamma_A\, A_{\text{std},i}.
$$

The observed count remains Beta-Binomial,

$$
B_{\text{post},i} \sim \operatorname{BetaBinomial}
\left(N,\mu_i\kappa,(1-\mu_i)\kappa\right), \qquad N=10,
$$

but the score mean is

$$
\mu_i = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{2}{3}\,\sigma(\eta_i),
$$

so it ranges from the chance performance of a three-alternative item to perfect performance. The ordinary companion uses $\mu_i=\sigma(\eta_i)$ and permits expected scores below chance. Systematic distractor choice could in principle produce below-chance performance, so the guessing floor is mechanically motivated rather than unquestionably true; this is why the two fits must be reported together. Although both models use the same latent-scale coefficient priors, the inverse link maps those priors to different distributions for the items-scale effect. The paired report therefore shows both prior pushforwards as well as both posteriors.

::: {.callout-important title="Interpret only as a paired sensitivity"}
The items-scale average marginal effect, its interval, direction probability and practical-significance probability are link-dependent. Release requires the content-addressed comparison bundle to prove that both reporting traces passed the clean all-variable gate and used the same children, treatment assignments, data, sampling contract and settings apart from `score_mean_link`. Do not select whichever link gives the more favourable result.
:::
